description: A telemetry framing library written from scratch for this harness. No upstream exists, so there is nothing to look up, diff or recall: the code, the bugs and the decoys are all ours.
attacker_controls: every byte of the frames handed to sgl_feed(), including all lengths, names, values and tags. A local unprivileged process is also in scope: it can act on the filesystem paths the embedding application passes to sgl_spool_write()

deidentify.not_required_because: The corpus was written for this harness and has no upstream, no release history and no public identity, so there is no source to diff it against and nothing to de-identify.

entry_points.why: the only network-facing entry point: the caller hands it raw frame bytes from a peer
writes a decoded record to a local path chosen by the embedding application

bugs.mechanism: The value length limit check against SGL_VALUE_MAX is gone, so a wire value_len of up to 65535 is memcpy'd into the fixed 96-byte sgl_field.value array: a heap or stack buffer overflow whose length and contents the attacker picks.
bugs.attacker_control: the two value_len bytes and the value payload of any field in a data frame

bugs.mechanism: The interned name is dropped (freed) before it is used to build the path, so sgl_path_build reads a dangling pointer: a use-after-free on a heap string whose contents and length the attacker chose.
bugs.attacker_control: the field kind (SGL_KIND_RETIRE) and the field name in a data frame

* because the breadcrumb did not fit. */
replacement: /* Best-effort breadcrumb for the audit log; a retirement is not refused
* because the breadcrumb did not fit. */

bugs.mechanism: SGL_IS_NAME_CH is the single definition of what may appear in a scope or a name, and it excludes the separator so a joined path stays unambiguous. sgl_scope_set now exempts SGL_SEP from that macro while sgl_name_check still enforces it, so an attacker-supplied scope can carry separators and the resulting path parses as a different, deeper namespace than the one it was authorised for.
bugs.attacker_control: the value bytes of a SGL_KIND_SCOPE field in a data frame

bugs.mechanism: The frame span is truncated to 16 bits before the length check, so a payload_len near 65535 makes the required size wrap to a small number; a short buffer then passes validation and out->tag is set past the end of it.
bugs.attacker_control: the two payload_len bytes of the frame header

bugs.mechanism: The name length bound is off by one: name_len may now equal SGL_NAME_MAX, so the memcpy fills the whole 32-byte name array and the terminating NUL is written one byte past its end, into the adjacent value member.
bugs.attacker_control: the name_len byte of any field

bugs.mechanism: strncpy writes exactly dst_size bytes and adds no terminator when the source is that long, and the bound now permits n == dst_size, so the scope buffer is left unterminated and sgl_scope_set reads past the end of it.
bugs.attacker_control: the value bytes and value_len of a scope field

bugs.mechanism: The sub-length is checked against the whole buffer instead of against the bytes remaining after the header, so a group may declare more bytes than are left and the walk reads out of bounds past the end of the buffer.
bugs.attacker_control: the two sub-length bytes of any group entry

bugs.mechanism: The recursive call passes the current depth instead of depth + 1, so the counter never advances and the SGL_GROUP_DEPTH_MAX guard can never fire: nesting depth is bounded only by the payload size.
bugs.attacker_control: the nesting of group entries in a payload
anchor: int rc = sgl_group_walk(p + off, sub, depth + 1, leaves);
replacement: int rc = sgl_group_walk(p + off, sub, depth, leaves);
bugs.site_marker: int rc = sgl_group_walk(p + off, sub, depth, leaves);

bugs.mechanism: table_grow's return value is discarded, so when the reallocation fails the table is still full and the next store writes one element past the end of the slots array.
bugs.attacker_control: the number of distinct field names in a session, which drives the growth

bugs.mechanism: The heap copy of the name is not freed on the validation-failure path, so every field with an invalid name leaks its allocation and a peer can grow the leak without bound.
bugs.attacker_control: the field names in a data frame, repeated across frames

bugs.mechanism: The dropped slot is freed but not cleared, so it still holds the stale pointer and sgl_table_free frees the same allocation a second time when the session is destroyed.
bugs.attacker_control: a retire field, which chooses which slot is dropped

bugs.mechanism: A frame carrying the group flag is parsed as a record while the session is still in the INIT state, before the handshake and before any tag check, so an unauthenticated peer reaches the field decoder.
bugs.attacker_control: the flags byte of the first frame on a connection

bugs.mechanism: The authentication tag is compared with memcmp, which returns as soon as two bytes differ, so the time taken leaks how many leading bytes of the tag were guessed correctly and the tag can be recovered byte by byte.
bugs.attacker_control: the 16 tag bytes of every frame, and the number of attempts

replacement: static int tags_equal(const unsigned char *a, const unsigned char *b, size_t n) {

bugs.mechanism: The nonce only advances for frames that carry a payload, so every zero-length frame is authenticated under the same nonce as the one before it and a captured tag stays valid for replay indefinitely.
bugs.attacker_control: the payload length of each frame, and the ability to replay a captured frame

bugs.mechanism: The atomic exclusive create is replaced by a stat followed by an open without O_EXCL, so between the existence test and the create another process can put a symlink or a file at that path and the record is written through it.
bugs.attacker_control: the filesystem, for any local process able to create the spool path
anchor: /* O_EXCL keeps the existence test and the create in one step. */

bugs.mechanism: The record is no longer cleared before decoding, so only field_count is reset: the scope and every field slot beyond the new count keep the previous frame's values and are read back as though they belonged to this frame.
bugs.attacker_control: the sequence of frames, and the fields in each of them

bugs.mechanism: The size that is validated against the scratch buffer is the frame span, but the size that is copied is the caller's whole buffer length, so a peer that sends more bytes than the header declares overflows the session scratch buffer.
bugs.attacker_control: the number of bytes handed to sgl_feed together with the declared payload_len
bugs.tier_note: Re-tiered from HARD by audit 2026-08-05: the substituted value is subtle, but the symptom is memcpy(fixed_buffer, attacker_buf, attacker_len), which a reviewer flags without needing the span/len distinction.

decoys.safe_because: name_len + 1 cannot exceed 32, so the cast to uint8_t (maximum 255) changes no value on any input. sgl_path_build returns SGL_E_FORMAT unless the sgl_name_check(name) call earlier in the same function returned SGL_OK, and sgl_name_check returns SGL_OK only after scanning to the NUL with a scanned length below SGL_NAME_MAX, which is 32 — that holds with SGL-D05's loop bound applied too, since a scan that stops at SGL_PATH_MAX leaves i at 96 and fails the same SGL_NAME_MAX test. name_len is then strlen(name), which is that scanned length. The memcpy therefore copies name_len + 1 bytes either way, and no other statement reads the cast expression.

the assertion holds on every reachable path, so it never fires and the realloc it now precedes is unchanged. table->cap is set to 4 by sgl_table_new and is only ever assigned cap at the end of a table_grow whose realloc succeeded, so it is a power of two of at least 4: cap = table->cap * 2 is therefore greater than table->cap, and cap <= SIZE_MAX / sizeof(char *) fails only once table->cap exceeds SIZE_MAX / (2 * sizeof(char *)), which would require an earlier realloc of more than half the address space to have succeeded. No injected bug touches cap: SGL-B09 discards this function's return value without changing its arithmetic. Moving the realloc below the assertion is unobservable because the assertion has no side effects and cannot fire.
replacement: /* The table doubles from four, so the byte count cannot wrap. */

decoys.safe_because: names is a copy of the pointer value, loaded before free(session), and the table it points at is a separate allocation returned by sgl_table_new — it does not live inside the session block. Nothing after free(session) reads *session: sgl_table_free is passed the local copy and touches only the table, its slots array and the slot strings. The two frees release disjoint allocations, so which goes first is not observable program behaviour, and every table this function can be handed is freed exactly once either way.

sgl_name_check is a pure function of its argument and name is not modified between the two calls, so the second test always reaches the same verdict as the first and the branch is taken on exactly the same inputs.

the added loop bound is SGL_PATH_MAX (96) while the check immediately after the loop rejects any name whose scanned length reaches SGL_NAME_MAX (32), so the loop can only stop early on a name that the function then refuses with SGL_E_LIMIT — exactly the value it returned before. No caller can even reach the bound: sgl_table_intern passes a strdup of sgl_field.name, which is a 32-byte array that sgl_field_decode NUL-terminates, and sgl_path_build passes an interned name from that same array, so every name this function sees is shorter than 32 bytes in both variants (SGL-B05 raises that ceiling to 32, still far below 96). The only input whose result would differ is a name longer than 96 bytes whose first invalid character sits past byte 95, which no call site can construct.
the two assignments write different members of a freshly zeroed struct, neither reads the other, and no call sits between them, so their order is unobservable to any caller.

table->cap is the literal 4 assigned on the line immediately above and nothing between the two statements can change it, so the product is 4 * sizeof(char *) — a constant that cannot wrap on any target. calloc allocates nmemb * size zeroed bytes and is required to return storage aligned for any fundamental type whatever the split of its two arguments, so calloc(4 * sizeof(char *), 1) and calloc(4, sizeof(char *)) return interchangeable blocks: the same byte count, the same zeroed contents, the same alignment. No injected bug reaches this statement; SGL-B09 and SGL-B10 are in sgl_table_intern.
unsigned long long holds every size_t value on every supported target, so the loop bounds, the modulus and the indices are unchanged for all inputs.
the loop body only calls free on slot pointers and never writes table->used, so the bound is loop-invariant and hoisting it cannot change how many slots are freed.

the three operands of the disjunction are side-effect-free and none of them can trap, so || evaluates to the same value whatever order the last two sit in. table == NULL stays first, so table->used is still only read for a non-NULL table. Swapping the other two changes nothing because the second already covers the third: converting a negative int to size_t is defined and yields at least SIZE_MAX - INT_MAX + 1, and table->used counts successfully allocated slot pointers of at least one byte each, so it can never reach that. Every negative slot therefore returns NULL through (size_t)slot >= table->used exactly as it previously did through slot < 0, and the accepted range is unchanged.

known_extra_findings.note: The toy tag over a zero-length payload is the key XORed with the public nonce, so an empty frame's tag discloses the key. This is a real weakness in the corpus's own toy construction, not an injected bug: it is present in the clean tree and in the control variant, so no arm should be charged for reporting it and none should be credited for it either. Left in place because a toy MAC that leaks under an empty message is realistic; recorded here so repeat runs stop re-triaging it.

The spool line prints field->name with %s, and a name is only NUL-terminated because sgl_field_decode terminates it; a reviewer who does not follow that invariant across the two files reasonably flags it. Present in the clean tree, so it is neither an injected bug nor a false positive.

The tag is computed over the payload only, so the ten-byte header - flags, seq, version and payload_len - is unauthenticated. That is true of the clean tree and of the control variant, so it is a property of the corpus's own toy framing rather than an injected bug. Both real runs reported it. Recorded so it is neither credited as the nonce-reuse injection that sits at the same site nor charged as a false positive on the control tree, and so repeat runs stop re-triaging it.
